A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the denoising auto-encoder is not the best way to learn a representation for a given set of inputs, and propose a simple modification that can lead to better results.
we have proposed a novel objective function for denoising auto-encoder that forces the auto-encoder to perform most of the denosing effort at the encoder stage.
we have shown that DAEs can be made to learn better representations by modifying their objective function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple modification to DAEs' objective function, that forces the denoising to occur mostly in the encoder's side, leads to better representations.
a simple modification of the original objective function of DAEs can result in a better representation, and this can be achieved without any changes to the architecture.
, in order to obtain a better representation, it is necessary to force the encoder to carry out most, if not all, the denoising.
